counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span mentions blistering, erosions, or skin fragility; the EB identifier appears only in the image titles.
No raw span documents congenital onset at birth, which would be needed for congenital melanocytic nevus.
No raw span demonstrates invasive melanoma or metastasis; the Myriad myPath result -7.1 is in the benign nevus range.

response.rationale: R5 wins because the supplied image titles verbatim name the exact diagnosis at two ages, while R4 only captures the biopsy-supported atypical nevus component without the syndrome-level EB-nevus label. R2 is contradicted by the benign gene-expression result; R3 lacks congenital-onset evidence; R6 lacks Ota topography.

rejected.why: Nevus of Ota requires facial/ocular dermal melanocytosis; the raw lesion is on the lateral ankle and no Ota-specific raw span exists.
This is an append-only completion of R4 based on the second biopsy; it adds dermal fibrosis but does not name the EB-nevus diagnosis and has less broad raw support than R4.
No raw span establishes congenital presence; the patch developed at age 6 and early care at age 4 does not prove congenital onset.
Melanoma is disconfirmed by the gene-expression result -7.1, which is explicitly in the benign nevus range; atypical histopath features alone are insufficient.
